header: Date: 2026-04-29 | Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: ~46 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Redwood Product), Carlos Martinez (Zenith Head of ML), Priya Nair (Zenith Eng Manager), Liam O'Connor (Zenith Platform)
summary: Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8) and quality vs latency tradeoffs. SE demo'd profile recommendations, quality regression monitoring, and example latency/unit-cost numbers. Customer wants bench on their dataset and clarity on Dedicated vs Hosted economics and security controls.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Um this is Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, with Samira our SE. We\'re gonna run through Optimize and the quant profiles, int8 and fp8, show quality vs latency slides and then talk next steps. Uh, Evan\'s on for product questions.
[00:18] Carlos Martinez: Hi thanks, yeah Carlos here. We are mainly concerned with keeping our NLU quality at parity while reducing inference costs for chat and retrieval. We run about 150 qps at peak now, kind of split between short prompts and long context scoring.
[00:32] Samira Khan: Great, Carlos. For context — when we say INT8 we mean per-tensor symmetric quantization typically, and FP8 is the newer reduced-precision format that preserves dynamic range better. On many LLM variants FP8 gives much better quality retention compared to naive int8, especially for long-context or sensitive generation. But INT8 often wins on latency and memory in certain runtimes.
[00:58] Priya Nair: When you say "wins on latency" do you mean p50 or p99? We care about p95 for user facing.
[01:07] Samira Khan: Good call. We typically look at p50, p95 and p99. In our Optimize profiles we surface p50 and p95 by default, and we can run p99 if you want the tail. INT8 tends to reduce p50 by 15-30% vs fp16 baseline on the GPUs we\'re targeting; FP8 can be a sweet spot — it often matches INT8 latency close while giving better quality, but results are model and prompt dependent.
[01:33] Liam O'Connor: Sorry quick question — is this applicable to our private deployment? We're evaluating Dedicated and Private (VPC) options.
[01:39] Jordan Lee: Yes — Optimize profiles are runtime-agnostic; they produce recommended kernel/quant combinations that the serving runtime will select. On Dedicated we can pin a profile and run large-scale benchmarks. On Private/VPC we support the same profiles, but we do need to validate kernel availability on your hardware; sometimes vendor drivers change performance.
[01:55] Carlos Martinez: Can you show concrete numbers? We have a baseline of fp16, avg latency 220ms p95 at our traffic mix.
[02:02] Samira Khan: Absolutely. I'll share my screen — deck link and spreadsheet are in the chat: https://redwood.ai/decks/optimize-zenith and https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/zenith-sample.
[02:16] [screen share — Samira presents slides]
[02:20] Samira Khan: Slide one — workflow: we profile your workload, recommend quant profile (e.g., int8 hybrid per-layer, or fp8 dynamic), run an A/B on a canary, then monitor quality via eval set and automatic regression alerts.
[02:35] Samira Khan: Here are example numbers from a comparable customer on A100s: fp16 baseline p95 220ms / cost $0.045 per 1k tokens (example), INT8 profile got p95 160ms with a 28% cost reduction, FP8 profile had p95 170ms with only a 6% quality delta on our evals.
[02:55] Priya Nair: "quality delta" — how are you measuring that?
[02:58] Samira Khan: Good question: we use a mixed metric — for generation tasks we run pairwise BLEU/ROUGE-ish plus human evals for a small set, and for classification/reranking we use accuracy and AUC. Optimize ties these to prompt sets and surfaces regression alerts. The deck shows the eval harness and thresholds.
[03:18] Evan Park: Also important — we tie quality monitoring to the rollout. If an INT8 canary trips the regression threshold, traffic automatically falls back to the previous profile. That keeps production apps safe.
[03:30] Carlos Martinez: Do you have any examples where INT8 caused failures we should worry about?
[03:35] Samira Khan: There are edge cases — hallucination rates increased on certain instruction-following prompts when quantizing aggressively. That's why we recommend a staged rollout and per-prompt eval sets. For Zenith's use case with multi-turn chat, FP8 often helps preserve the coherence while still improving cost.
[03:52] Liam O'Connor: What about KV cache implications for long context? We do a lot of retrieval-augmented generation with long KV caching.
[03:58] Samira Khan: Good point. Quantization affects KV storage size and cache hits — INT8 reduces the KV footprint which can improve throughput for long context, but rounding can introduce small drift in logits over many steps; FP8 tends to keep that drift lower. We can instrument the KV error over sequence length in the bench.
[04:20] [timestamp jump — demo continues]
[04:25] Samira Khan: Now the Optimize UI demo — you can see profiles listed per-model, each with expected latency and estimated quality delta vs baseline. You can create a profile for a specific route, set rollout percentages, and attach an eval corpus.
[04:40] Samira Khan: Note the "safety net" policies — automatic rollback and fallback to compatible model variants (e.g., fallback to a fp16 small shard) to avoid outages.
[04:50] Priya Nair: For us, security is key. How do you handle keys and audit logs during Dedicated or Private?
[04:56] Jordan Lee: We support KMS/HSM integrations on Private and Dedicated. Audit logs include token-level request traces (obfuscated) and we can retain logs per your retention policies. We also offer SOC 2 and ISO docs; I'll send the security packet.
[05:12] Carlos Martinez: Are you able to support our compliance team with the SOC2 statements quickly? We have an auditor we work with.
[05:17] Jordan Lee: Yes — I'll connect you to our compliance lead; we often provide an auditor pack. I'll include contact details in the follow-up.
[05:26] Samira Khan: Back to latency — here's a heatmap for different sequence lengths. For short prompts (<=64 tokens) INT8 gives big wins on p50 and p95. For long sequences (>1024) FP8 often offers a better quality-latency ratio.
[05:42] Carlos Martinez: Hmm our mix is 70% short prompts but the 30% long ones are the highest value users. We can't sacrifice those.
[05:50] Samira Khan: That's common — Optimize lets you route by policy, e.g., short prompt route uses INT8; long-context route pins FP8. We can also set per-route rollouts so high-value traffic stays on safer profiles.
[06:04] [crosstalk — brief interruptions]
[06:08] Liam O'Connor: Do you support automatic batching with quant profiles? Our p95 is spiky and batching helps considerably.
[06:14] Samira Khan: Yes — the runtime's batching heuristics still apply. Optimize recommends batch sizes and kernel choices per profile. For INT8 we may choose kernels that are batching-optimized; for FP8 we might pick different ones.
[06:26] Priya Nair: Who owns the cost assumptions in the spreadsheet? I want a clear expected unit-cost delta for budgeting.
[06:33] Jordan Lee: We'll provide example unit-cost math in the follow-up spreadsheet — it includes GPU-hour, amortized infra, kernel speed ups, and expected token cost. We'll run that against your traffic shape once you share traces.
[06:46] Carlos Martinez: What's the timeline for the bench? We need results before committing to Dedicated in June.
[06:51] Jordan Lee: If you can send sample traces and a ~5k prompt eval set this week, Samira can run the bench and we can have results in about a week. That aligns with a POC kickoff in mid-May.
[07:03] Samira Khan: I'll also include the exact commands we use for profiling so your platform team can reproduce locally if needed.
[07:10] [timestamp — mid-call deeper technical dive]
[07:14] Carlos Martinez: For the evaluation, can you run both automatic metrics and a small human evaluation? We want to ensure subjective quality for our 30% long prompts.
[07:21] Samira Khan: Yes — we recommend a mixed approach: automatic metrics for broad coverage and a 50–100 sample human review for the long-context high-value cases. We can recruit reviewers or you can provide internal SMEs.
[07:34] Priya Nair: Any specific gotchas with prompt engineering and quant profiles? We do a lot of system prompts.
[07:40] Samira Khan: System prompts are sensitive — aggressive quantization sometimes affects token probabilities that are primarily influenced by system instructions. We recommend including system prompts in the eval corpus. Also consider reranking the top-k with a small fp16 re-ranker if you need extra safety.
[07:55] Evan Park: One feature to call out — Optimize can do targeted conservative quantization where earlier layers stay fp16/fp32 and later layers are quantized; that's good for preserving instruction-following.
[08:08] Liam O'Connor: Performance on our on-prem X-series machines… any surprises?
[08:13] Samira Khan: Hardware variance matters. We'll validate kernels on your exact driver stack. Some vendor-specific FP8 paths are still new and may need driver patches. We document compatibility in the ticket we open for your infra team.
[08:26] [pause — Jordan types in chat link to compatibility matrix]
[08:30] Jordan Lee: Link to compatibility matrix: https://redwood.ai/compatibility. Note the FP8 kernel maturity varies by GPU vendor.
[08:40] Carlos Martinez: If FP8 kernel isn't mature on our hardware, what fallback?
[08:44] Samira Khan: Then Optimize will recommend INT8 hybrid or a mixed profile, or fall back to fp16 with different batching. The rollout will automatically route to a safe variant.
[08:54] Priya Nair: Ok — let's look at the POC scope now.
[08:57] Jordan Lee: Proposed POC: 4 weeks benching + 6 week integration + ramp. Phase 1 — Samira runs bench on sample traces and eval set; Phase 2 — Dedicated pilot with pinned profiles and monitoring; Phase 3 — roll to prod. We can shorten or lengthen based on results.
[09:18] Carlos Martinez: Budget-wise — when do we need to commit? We have a procurement cycle in mid-June.
[09:23] Jordan Lee: If we can show >20% unit-cost reduction with no more than 3% quality delta on your metrics we can justify Dedicated commit. We can also do a shorter contract for initial Dedicated bundles.
[09:34] Priya Nair: Any surprises on data residency? We have EU users and want EU-only hosting for those customers.
[09:40] Jordan Lee: We support region pinning and data residency policies on Hosted and Dedicated; Private is entirely customer-managed so that's easiest for strict residency.
[09:49] Carlos Martinez: Can you confirm log retention options? Our security policy wants 90-day request logs.
[09:54] Jordan Lee: Yes, configurable retention: 30/90/365 days and exportable to your SIEM. We'll include retention options in the follow-up.
[10:05] [later — Samira shows benchmark run commands and a short live run]
[10:10] Samira Khan: Running a quick sample — you'll see throughput increase when switching to INT8 on this small model, and FP8 keeps the quality closer to baseline. Remember transcription artifacts: some customers see micro-differences in punctuation, but semantic quality is preserved.
[10:30] Priya Nair: Are there licensing implications for any of these kernels? Some vendors have license terms for optimized libraries.
[10:36] Jordan Lee: Good catch — we will surface any third-party kernel license constraints in the compatibility doc. Typically those are Apache/BSD but sometimes vendors have specific terms. We'll highlight anything that affects deployment.
[10:50] Carlos Martinez: Ok folks, sounds good. Quick ask: can you provide a sample benchmark output and the Optimize profile JSON we would apply? We need it for our infra team.
[10:58] Samira Khan: Yes — Samira: I'll export the profile and the bench CSV. Note that the export includes kernel hints and rollout configs. Link after call.
[11:08] Jordan Lee: Recap — Samira runs the bench on Zenith data and shares results by 2026-05-06; Jordan shares pricing and SOC2 pack; Liam provides sample traces and infra constraints; Carlos confirms POC timeline.
[11:20] Carlos Martinez: Great, thanks everyone.
[11:23] [00:11:23 end — call concludes with scheduling a follow-up demo next week if bench shows promising results]
